issues.reason: Existential reserves the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object and bars it 'for a specific definite individual', so the definite subject 'The mist-light' of a dated past attracting event may not be filled by mist_light -- the very symbol the parse also uses kind-side in (Inheritance mist_light light).

The coherence half stands -- the survivors had just fled to and reached the Hollows while the threads sit on the Harbor Row lanterns, so the Harbor Row crowd is the better antecedent -- but the error half does not: Coreference resolves 'to the most salient compatible antecedent (gender/number agreement + recency)', which licenses the just-mentioned sk_nightmoth_2, and since those moths were at the Harbor Row before fleeing no emitted atom is false.

gaps_confirmed: Ordinal day-of-year dating in a non-Gregorian calendar ('on day 300 of Year 1'): (Day <n>) is the day-of-month slot, with no term for a bare day-number of a year.

Bare 'together' over a definite plural encoded as one group witness: the collective form is defined as one event with multiple Agent atoms, which a single group symbol cannot express, so 'together' leaves no positive trace -- its only record is the absence of the per-member distribution rule.
new_gaps: A definite mass anaphor whose antecedent entered the KB as a bare mass constant ('the lanterns produced mist-light' ... 'The mist-light attracted nightmoths'): the episodic bare-plural-object rule has no mass analogue, so the definite witness the Existential rule demands would sit unlinked to the mass that was produced and shown, and no identity link between witness and bare kind constant is licensed.
defect_summary: Issue 0: the compliant form types the definite mass as its own individual -- (Member sk_mist_light_1 mist_light) with (Agent sk_attract_1 sk_mist_light_1) -- but nothing licenses tying that witness to the mist_light the two earlier episodic clauses stored as a bare constant, which is the gap filed above.
notes: Unflagged by the reviewer: (Patient sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1) should be Theme -- leaving threads on the lanterns displaces them without changing them, the same test that gives 'slid the plate off the counter' a Theme. The 'at the Harbor Row' attachment onto the crowd NP is a defensible commitment rather than an unmarked ambiguity, since the next sentence repeats the same restrictor on the same NP.
